gpu_private_tests: GPU leases bound pool and survive reuse/resize/retirement, odd padding
Encoder preference restores classic capture while retaining old GPU pixels
private_functional: Reconnect preserves original fixture and starts IDR
Six static windows publish through four private GPU targets
125%/100%/125% scaling, 2x source controls, nested popup geometry and padding
injected_errors: First GPU input failure uses software before first publication
Midstream GPU failure starts new software stream and IDR
policy_tests: GPU latency gain and later contention
Small/negative gain and failure do not loop

unsuccessful_attempts: An early CPU comparison failed the former all-frame source counter association; incomplete ABBA excluded
Single IDR OpenH264 drain check failed; FFmpeg independently decoded it; SPS has max_num_reorder_frames=0 and DPB=2. Continuous OpenH264 streams pass
One full GNOME smoke attempt failed an existing panned-pointer stage-bound check; dedicated video/scaling checks pass
Intermediate default GPU and latency-only choices regressed under some GPU loads; all valid pairs retained
An instrumentation generation failed on Python string concatenation; corrected before any associated build/measurement

deployment.hardware_policy: automatic; compare CPU/GPU and restore classic capture when software selected

limitations: Only this local Intel system and test-owned workloads were measured
No actual user application captured or input injected; no user profile/account files read
No QUIC or remote decode/display latency measurement; not a universal 26% improvement
Short automatic probes are conservative estimates and cannot ensure the best path during arbitrary changing load
GPU encoding skips CPU exact-pixel dedup; CPU modes retain it
OpenH264 single-picture EOS behavior differs from FFmpeg; no new macOS decoder validation
Private VPP converts and GPU fences still wait; this is avoidance of CPU pixel roundtrip, not full zero-copy
